title: Client latency budgeting, model mapping & calibration notes
content:
Context and goal:
This is a working capture from the customer workshop (FinTech pilot) focused on: (1) sizing a latency budget end-to-end, (2) mapping candidate model variants to the customer’s inferred latency/cost targets, and (3) a short calibration checklist for quantization + prompt/pipeline tuning.

Status: quick field notes after 2024-06-10 workshop. We ran mini benchmarks on cpu/gpu footprints; this doc collects heuristics, flagged unknowns, and an actionable experiment list for SE and infra.

Customer constraints / ask:
- 95th percentile response time target: 300 ms for single-turn customer queries (avg prompt length ~180 tokens).
- Max allowed inference cost target: equivalent to ~30M tokens / month at their committed spend (we translated to per-request target ~0.6c/request, approximate).
- Data sensitivity: PII allowed in private deployment; they prefer Private (VPC) or Dedicated.
- Peak concurrency: expected burst of 200 qps sustained for 5 minutes; steady 10–20 qps.

Top-candidate model families we considered:
- Alpaca-7B / LLaMA-variant 7B (float16 -> 4-bit quantizable)
- Mistral-instruct-ish 7B family (dense; promising perf on GPU kernels)
- 3B distilled variant for fallback/low-cost lane

Mapping heuristics (rough):
- Latency baseline: unquantized 7B on A100: ~80–120ms per 1-token? (depends on prefix KV reuse). For 180-token prompt + 20-token generation, end-to-end inference dominated by decode loop; continuous batching/windowing vital.
- 4-bit quantized 7B on T4/3090-like: expected 1.6–2x decode latency reduction vs fp16 on same card; cost drop ~40–55% (kernel-dependent).
- Distilled 3B on CPU-hosted Dedicated (heavy batching): latency may hit 250–350ms depending on batch strategy; not reliable for p95 under burst.

KV cache strategy and prompt shaping notes:
- Encourage prefix caching for user context that is repeated across calls (session templates). That reduced token work by ~25% in our bench.
- For prompts > 150 tokens, measure prefill time separately — prefill dominates for long contexts; consider offline caching of static system/instruction blocks.
- For customer use-case, experiment: strip explicit examples from prompt and store as ephemeral context blob referenced by short pointer (reduce tokens sent).

Quantization considerations and calibration checklist:
1) Data sensitivity check: does quantization affect determinism for auditability? For this customer, they want reproducible regression tests at rollout — include seed + deterministic decoding in CI.
2) Calibration dataset: use 1k in-domain prompts (sampled from their staging logs). Keep 20% edge-case examples.
3) Calibration runs: run 4-bit symmetric and asymmetric quant runs; measure: token-level perplexity proxy, exact-match on 200 eval prompts, and human-judged fidelity on 50 samples.
4) Fallback triggers: If accuracy regression > 6% (on fidelity rubric), do not deploy quantized as primary; use as fallback lane for cost-savings with lower SLO.
5) Kernel selection: prefer Triton-backed kernels where available; if unsupported, fall back to custom fused kernels in runtime branch.

Prompt/pipeline tuning heuristics:
- Chunking long inputs: use semantic sentence splits rather than fixed token windows to avoid context loss.
- Prefix condensation: compress system instructions to one-liners where safe; keep examples in a separate few-shot buffer that we can swap (reduces prompt tokens).
- Temperature / sampling: align eval metric for customer (they prefer conservative answers) -> temperature 0.0–0.2 and operator-level postfilters for hallucination cases.

Benchmark matrix to run (priority order):
- A: 7B fp16 (A100) vs 7B 4-bit (A100/T4) on 180-token prompt + 20-token gen. Metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-request, top-1 fidelity.
- B: 3B distilled 4-bit on Dedicated CPU vs small GPU for baseline cost lane.
- C: KV cache effectiveness test: repeated-session vs cold-start p95.
- D: Batch sizing sweep: 1,2,4,8 for p95 under 200 qps burst simulation.

Experiment schedule (2-week sprint):
- Week 1: run A and C in lab using customer sample set; collect telemetry + trace. Create PR with kernel/runtime flags.
- Week 2: run B & D; prepare calibration artifacts; run small human eval for fidelity.

Open questions / risks identified:
- Kernel availability on customer-preferred hardware (customer prefers on-prem 3080 nodes) — need runtime team check on fused 4-bit kernel support. (Action: @Ravi to file infra check ticket).
- Quantized model nondeterminism with beam search edge-cases — need stress tests in CI.
- Cost model mismatch: their finance team calculates token-cost using different tokenization (we used tiktoken-like). Reconcile with sample bill.

Quick wins to propose to customer in next call:
- Turn on prefix KV caching for session-heavy flows (easy config in Redwood Console) — expect immediate p95 improvement for repeat users.
- Run a 1-week calibration project: we deliver 1k-cal dataset, run 4-bit calibration, and present fidelity tradeoffs with a small cost forecast.

Notes / links from the workshop:
- Workshop recording: internal drive (link attached in Confluence page).
- Slack thread: #se-fintech-pilot — highlights pinned by @Sofia.

Next steps (action owners):
- Ethan: run the A100 vs T4 bench (deadline 2024-06-18) and upload raw traces.
- Sofia: assemble 1k calibration dataset from staging logs (deadline 2024-06-20).
- Ravi: confirm 4-bit kernel support for customer 3080 on-prem fleet (create infra ticket by 2024-06-16).
- Maya: draft customer-facing one-pager with latency-budget diagram and proposed AB rollout plan (draft by 2024-06-14).

Small working checklist for SE demo deploy:
- [ ] Confirm model files are compatible with assembly/quant tooling
- [ ] Create two model variants in console (primary fp16, fallback 4-bit)
- [ ] Add canary routing rule at 5% traffic for quantized lane
- [ ] Add metrics alert on p95 latency delta > 20% or fidelity regression > 5%

Appendix: quick metric definitions we used in notes:
- p50/p95: 50th/95th percentile end-to-end request latency (client observed).
- prefill: time to process static prompt prefix + system tokens before decode loop.
- decode-loop: per-token generation time after prefill.

End of notes. This doc = working artifact; expect follow-up edits as we accumulate bench outputs and customer feedback.

Unresolved sync: need to align with runtime team on quant kernel rollout timeline (blocking) and create an infra pairing session next week.
